"Someone I loved found out." The look on her face hurt more than any streak reset.

carousels.name: Secret p*rn use and your own intimacy (2023 study)

slides.title: Watching p*rn behind your partner's back? [[Researchers found it hits YOUR closeness that day.]]
What they [[measured]]
slides.body: Vaillancourt-Morel and colleagues tracked couples day by day and looked at p*rn use the partner didn't know about.

slides.title: The [[finding]]
slides.body: On days people used p*rn secretly, they themselves reported lower relationship satisfaction and intimacy that day. The effect was short-term — but it showed up day after day it happened.

slides.title: Why that [[makes sense]]
slides.body: Hiding something creates distance. You feel it before she ever does. Secret p*rn quietly turns your partner into someone you're managing.

slides.title: Close the [[distance]]
items: Notice how you feel around her after secret p*rn.
Stop the hiding — that's what creates the gap.
Talk about boundaries you both agree on.
Get support if you can't stop on your own.

carousels.name: 6 signs p*rn has crept into how you talk about women

slides.title: 6 signs p*rn has crept into [[how you talk about women.]]
slides.sub: It doesn't stay on the screen.

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: You rate women out loud like they're content.
Your jokes sound like p*rn titles.
You describe women by body parts first.

slides.title: Signs [[4–6]]
items: You assume what women "want" based on what you've watched.
You laugh along when friends talk about women like objects.
You'd be embarrassed if a woman you respect heard it.

slides.title: Language [[shapes]] you.
slides.body: The way you talk about women trains how you see them — and how you treat them. P*rn writes the script. You don't have to read it.

slides.title: Change the [[script]]
items: Catch yourself mid-sentence.
Say less about bodies, more about people.
Don't laugh along — silence speaks.
Quit p*rn and notice what changes.

slides.title: You deleted the app. You'll reinstall it in 3 days. [[That's not quitting p*rn — that's a ritual.]]
The delete [[high]]
slides.body: Deleting feels like action. It feels like a fresh start. It's the easiest part of quitting p*rn — and the least important.

slides.title: The [[reinstall]]
slides.body:
Three days later: bored, tired, "just to check one thing."

Many people on Reddit describe exactly this loop with social media and p*rn.

slides.title: Change the [[reason]], not the app
slides.body: If nothing about your evenings, your feelings or your reasons changes, the app comes back every time.

slides.title: Break the [[ritual]]
items: Ask why you go back — boredom? loneliness?
Replace the time, not just the app.
Let someone else hold your app-store password.
Count reinstalls — be honest with the number.
